players.note: George Pickens is the WR9 in fantasy points per game with a 22.5% target share, 2.23 YPRR, ten red zone targets, 18 deep targets, and a 26.6% first-read share. Pickens should have another standout week against the Eagles. Since Week 5, Philly has had the eighth-highest single-high rate (57.4%). Pickens continues to shred single-high with a 35% TPRR and 3.07 YPRR. Over their last five games, Philly has ranked 15th in yards per target while allowing the seventh-most receiving fantasy points per game to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 7, Cam Skattebo has been the RB10 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.6 touches and 97 total yards with a 76.6% snap rate. Among 55 qualifying backs, Skattebo is 25th in yards after contact per attempt and 24th in missed tackle rate. Skattebo should have another strong outing against the Colts. Across their last five games, Indy has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the sixth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the 11th-most yards after contact per attempt.

Ok, let's start this conversation off the right way. I'm worried about Chris Olave this week because he could easily see a shadow from DJ Turner. Turner has followed DK Metcalf (twice), Chris Bell, Emeka Egbuka, Parker Washington, Calvin Ridley, and Drake London on 56.7-86.2% of their routes. Metcalf is the only receiver to score against him (twice), but both instances were flukes. One of which Turner ran into a teammate and the other was when he fell. None of these receivers surpassed 55 receiving yards in Turner's coverage. Olave is the WR12 in fantasy points per game with a 25.1% target share, 2.25 YPRR, eight red zone targets, 22 deep targets, and a 35.4% first-read share. I'm not debating Olave's talent, but I won't expect a big day from the talented wideout in Week 12 if Turner is lined up against him the entire game.

Garrett Wilson is the WR21 in fantasy points per game with a 27.2% target share, 2.15 YPRR, nine red zone targets, 13 deep targets, and a 33.8% first-read share. I expect Wilson to crush this week. Miami still has no clue how to stop perimeter wide receivers. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the seventh-most yards per target and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

In his last two games, Saquon Barkley has been Philly's workhorse again with a 61.2% snap rate, 58.8% of the rushing work, and a 34.7% route share (1.8% target share WOOF!). Barkley has been a zero in the passing game with only one target in those two contests. In his last two games, Barkley has averaged 15 touches and 48.5 total yards. If (or when) Dallas pulls away from Philly on the scoreboard, Barkley could get gamescripted out of the contest. If Philly can keep it somewhat close, Barkley should have success on the ground. Among 55 qualifying rushers, Barkley is 27th in explosive run rate, 31st in yards after contact per attempt, and 34th in missed tackle rate. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 11th-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, the most yards after contact per attempt, and the tenth-highest missed tackle rate. Barkley could be a solid RB2 this week, but it's also possible that he produces a middling flex stat line again.

Breece Hall is back to being New York's workhorse back. Last week, he had a 62.7% snap rate with 54.1% of the rushing work and a 60.9% route share (14.3% target share). He finished with 23 touches, 100 total yards, and a score as the RB8 for the week. Hall's per-touch numbers remain uninspiring, though, as he has only 1.74 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate. Hall should have another strong week, though. Miami's run defense remains pitiful. Over their last five games, they have allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the tenth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

In his first game with Joe Milton under center, DeVonta Smith might have only produced 41 receiving yards, but he had elite usage. Smith had a 47.6% target share with 1.95 YPRR, two deep targets, and a 55.6% first-read share. If Smith gets this type of usage again this week, he could have a surprising stat line if Milton can get him catchable targets. Speaking of catchable targets, only 50% of Smith's targets were catchable last week. Across their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

The last time Tony Pollard faced this defense, he was the RB8 for the week, but that was mainly on the strength of nine targets, eight receptions, and 66 receiving yards. All of those receiving marks were massive outliers when compared against the rest of Pollard's season, so I'm not expecting that to happen again. Since Week 7, Pollard has been the RB3 in fantasy points per game with a 77.4% snap rate and 22.5 touches and 125.3 total yards per game. Among 55 qualifying rushers, Pollard is 23rd in explosive run rate, sixth in yards after contact per attempt, and 23rd in missed tackle rate. Pollard will need the passing game usage this week because he won't have much room on early downs to operate. Across their last six games, the Jags have allowed the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, the 13th-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the third-lowest EPA per attempt.

Since Week 8, Jonathan Taylor has been the RB35 in fantasy points per game, averaging 15.8 touches and 60.3 total yards. During these four games, Taylor has had a 67% snap rate, 48% of the rushing workload, and a 66.7% route share (16.5% target share). With Seth McGowan hurt, Taylor could see his snaps rise, but with Anthony Richardson under center, I'm expecting his target share to dip. Taylor has posted a strong 13% explosive run rate and an 18% missed tackle rate this season. He'll have uphill sledding this week against an improved Giants run defense. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the sixth-lowest rushing success rate, the seventh-fewest rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the fifth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the third-lowest missed tackle rate.

Over the last two games, Derrick Henry has been the RB11 and RB7 in weekly scoring (PPR). In those games, he has averaged 16 touches and 65.5 total yards. The elevated passing game usage has been nice, as he has had nine receptions and 27 receiving yards in these two contests. Overall, among 55 qualifying backs, Henry is 21st in explosive run rate and 19th in yards after contact per attempt. Henry should cook this week in a surprisingly good matchup. Houston's run defense has recently faltered. Over their last five games, they have allowed the eighth-highest rushing success rate, the 13th-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the seventh-highest missed tackle rate.

With Michael Penix under center, Drake London has been the WR14 in fantasy points per game. London has been doing so entirely on volume because during this stretch he has scored only one touchdown. Since Week 3, London has had a 26.5% target share with 3.08 YPRR, only four red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 35.6% first-read share. London is a volume-driven WR2 with a bad matchup this week. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position.

Since Week 7, Jaylen Warren has been the RB22 in fantasy points per game with a 56.6% snap rate, 48.1% of the rushing work, and a 41.2% route share (10.7% target share). In this span, he has averaged 15.6 touches and 87.6 total yards while splitting the red zone rushing work evenly with Rico Dowdle, with each back seeing seven red zone rushing attempts. Among 55 qualifying rushers, he is 16th in explosive run rate, 14th in yards after contact per attempt, and 11th in missed tackle rate. I hope this week Pittsburgh doesn't get drunk and allow Aaron Rodgers to drop back to pass constantly and instead leans on their rushing attack. If they do so, Warren will have a strong game. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, Mike Evans made his triumphant return as the WR4 for the week. Evans had a 57.1% route share with a 25.9% target share, 109 receiving yards (6.81 YPRR), one red zone target, two deep targets, and a 36.8% first-read share. Overall, Evans is the WR14 in fantasy points per game with a 23.2% target share, 4.04 YPRR (WOW!), seven red zone targets, 12 deep targets, and a 28.5% first-read share. The last time Evans faced Seattle, he destroyed them with seven receptions, 115 receiving yards, and 26.5 fantasy points as the WR5 for the week. I will not bet against Evans and the fact that he could do it again. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. I'm betting on Evans' talent winning out again in Week 12.

Since Week 4, Ollie Gordon has been the RB27 in fantasy points per game, averaging 18.3 touches and 86.6 total yards. Among 55 qualifying rushers, he is eighth in explosive run rate, 39th in yards after contact per attempt, and 33rd in missed tackle rate. His efficiency metrics have begun to slip over the last few weeks, which is notable because his offensive line is doing its job, providing him the eighth-most yards before contact per attempt among those 55 backs. Gordon should produce RB2/3 level production this week. The Jets' run defense has remained Swiss cheese. Over their last five games, they have allowed the ninth-highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, the third-highest explosive run rate, and the second-most yards before contact per attempt.

Last week, Ashton Jeanty reclaimed his bellcow role with an 86.4% snap rate with 45.8% of the rushing work, a 68.2% route share, and a 16.2% target share. Since Week 9, he has averaged 13.4 touches and 84.4 total yards as the RB15 in fantasy points per game. In these three games, he has had 2.58 yards after contact per attempt and a 12% missed tackle rate. The jump in yards after contact per attempt is nice to see. Jeanty should run wild again this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the second-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest yards after contact per attempt, and the second-highest missed tackle rate.

Tetairoa McMillan is dealing with a foot issue, but he enters this week's game without an injury designation. T Mac had limited practices on Friday and Saturday. Since Week 7, he has been the WR29 in fantasy points per game with a 21.6% target share, 1.61 YPRR, four red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 28.3% first-read share. McMillan is a WR2/3 again this week. He has a tough matchup to overcome, as this pass defense will impact the quality of targets he sees from Bryce Young. Over their last five games, the Bucs have allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position.

Jakobi Meyers is the WR47 in fantasy points per game (PPR) with five outings of at least double-digit PPR points. Meyers has a 16.5% target share with 1.93 YPRR, 13 red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 20.5% first-read share. With Parker Washington out this week. Meyers should operate as the Jags WR1. Meyers is a strong flex option this week. The Titans continue to have issues defending perimeter wide receivers. In their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Quinshon Judkins is the RB22 in fantasy points per game, averaging 16.8 touches and 65.8 total yards. Judkins has rushed for more than 60 yards only twice this season. He hasn't had 20 carries in a game all season. Since Week 7, with Dylan Sampson back, Judkins has had only a 17.5% route share and a 5.4% target share. Relying on his early-down prowess only is tough for Judkins, as he has produced only a 6% explosive run rate, 1.74 yards after contact per attempt, and a 13% missed tackle rate. That might not matter this week, though. The Raiders have had a pitiful run defense all season. Over their last five games, they have allowed the seventh-highest explosive run rate, the highest rushing success rate, the fourth-most yards before contact per attempt, and the 12th-most yards after contact per attempt.

Over the last two weeks, Omarion Hampton has been the RB13 and RB19 in weekly scoring. Since Week 10, Hampton has averaged 19 touches and 99 total yards. In these games, he has had a 60.4% snap rate, a 56.3% rushing share, and a 35.6% route share (7.7% target share). Hampton has been awesome with Mike McDaniel finally pulling his head out of his butt and utilizing Hampton the way that he should be. In these last two games, Hampton has an 18.2% explosive run rate and 2.97 yards after contact per attempt. 55.6% of his runs have been gap runs where he is ripping 6.35 yards per carry. The Bolts could lean on Hampton again this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the 13th-highest explosive run rate, the 14th-highest rushing success rate, and the third-most yards before contact per attempt.

Carnell Tate is the WR28 in fantasy points per game. Last week, in his return, he was the WR22 in weekly scoring, but much of that production came on a play where Dallas thought they had touched him after he hit the ground, but they were wrong, and Tate got up and rumbled for a massive gain. Last week, Tate had only a 13.3% target share with 58 receiving yards (2.15 YPRR), one red zone target, and an 18.8% first-read share (second on the team). I expect that to be more of an outlier than his usage moving forward. Overall this season, Tate has a 23.1% target share with 2.19 YPRR, four red zone targets, seven deep targets, and a 31% first-read share. Tate will have a tough day, though. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the 14th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Tate is a volume-driven flex only this week.

Since Week 7, Stefon Diggs has been the WR23 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 7, Diggs has had a 20.5% target share with 1.92 YPRR, four red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 22.3% first-read share. Last week, he took a step back as the WR2 for the offense with a 17.1% target share and 18.2% first-read share as Antonio Williams led the way. Diggs is a strong WR2 this week. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

KC Concepcion is the WR39 in fantasy points per game with four games of at least 11.4 PPR points. Concepcion has an 18.4% target share with 1.52 YPRR, four red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 26.1% first-read share. Concepcion has added to his fantasy output with some rushing usage, with at least 15 rushing yards twice this season and a rushing score. Concepcion should cook this week. Over their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the third-most yards per target and the second-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Since DJ Moore's return in Week 8, he has been the WR13 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 8, Moore has had a 21.2% target share with 2.72 YPRR, six red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 28.7% first-read share. Moore has been Buffalo's alpha WR1. The Chiefs have the seventh-highest two-high rate in the NFL (59.2%). Since Week 8, against two-high, Moore has had a 22% TPRR with 2.36 YPRR. Moore doesn't have an easy matchup this week, but in a big game as Allen's go-to, I'm willing to bet on talent that Moore will rise above the tough matchup. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

In his last game of action, Rhamondre Stevenson wasn't 100% as he played 43.6% of the snaps with a 27.3% rushing share and 27.8% route share (3.6% target share). Stevenson finished with seven touches and five total yards. That game was a blowout, so it easily could have impacted Stevenson's volume. In Weeks 1-9. Stevenson averaged 14.2 touches and 72 total yards. He easily could see a workload closer to that average this week. Among 55 qualifying backs, Stevenson is 35th in yards after contact per attempt and ninth in missed tackle rate. Stevenson is a risky flex who could produce an RB2 stat line this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the seventh-highest rushing success rate, the ninth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the ninth-most yards after contact per attempt.

With Bhayshul Tuten ruled out, Chris Rodriguez will handle lead back duties for Jacksonville this week. This season, among 55 qualifying backs, Rodriguez has been efficient with his work, ranking 18th in yards after contact per attempt and 20th in missed tackle rate. I expect Rodriguez to see some passing game work this week and handle 15-20 carries. As a big favorite, Rodriguez should see a solid dose of volume with a wonderful matchup. He's a rock-solid RB2 with RB1 upside this week. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the sixth-highest explosive run rate, the third-highest rushing success rate, and the tenth-most yards after contact per attempt.

In his last game played, Zach Charbonnet took over the backfield as the RB26 for the week. Charbonnet had a season-high 72.7% snap rate with a 57.1% rushing share and a 54.5% route share (zero targets). He finished with 20 carries and 94 rushing yards. He has been quite good on a per-touch basis this season with 2.93 yards after contact per attempt and a 17% missed tackle rate. Charbonnet will need all of the volume he can get this week to follow up with another strong game. San Francisco's run defense has been elite this season. Over their last five games, they have allowed the lowest explosive run rate, the fifth-lowest rushing success rate, the fourth-fewest yards after contact per attempt, and the third-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Rashee Rice is the WR29 in fantasy points per game. Since Week 10, he has had a 54.4% route share, a 16% target share (28% TPRR), 3.14 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 19.2% first-read share. Over those two games, he has been the WR26 in fantasy points per game. Last week, Rice saw his route share drop to 48.8% while having a 15% target share (30% TPRR), 53 receiving yards (2.65 YPRR), two red zone targets, and a 19.4% first-read share. Rice has a tough matchup this week, but with how Patrick Mahomes is playing, I wouldn't be shocked to see Rice overcome it. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the eighth-fewest yards per target and the third-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Travis Etienne was the RB27 in weekly scoring. He had a 45.1% snap rate, 63.6% of the rushing workload, and a 25% route share (zero targets). Etienne had 14 rushing attempts and 76 rushing yards. Etienne still didn't look fully healthy, though. He broke a long run last week that normally we'd see him house for a touchdown, but he seemed to run out of gas in the open field as he was ultimately tackled before the goal line. In his last two games, he has had only a 5% explosive run rate and a 9% missed tackle rate, so those numbers are telling a similar story. Much like the Bears' struggling run defense last week, maybe Cincy's horrible run defense can help prop him up this week. Etienne is a flex with RB2 upside. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the second-highest rushing success rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the 12th-highest missed tackle rate.

Last week, David Montgomery was the clear workhorse for Houston, finishing with a 72.3% snap rate, 70.3% of the rushing work, and a 54.8% route share (14.8% target share). Montgomery finished with 29 touches and 124 total yards as the RB13 for the week. We'll see if that type of workload holds this week with Woody Marks likely back. I expect Montgomery to lead the way for the backfield, but I don't know if Houston will give him that large of a share of the workload this week. Last week, Montgomery looked finally like the guy that Houston thought they were bringing in with a 15.4% explosive run rate and 2.58 yards after contact per attempt. Montgomery will need all the volume that he can get this week with a tough matchup incoming. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the ninth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt and missed tackle rate, and the fifth-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Over the last two weeks, Caleb Douglas has had a 25.8% target share with 1.77 YPRR, 50.5 receiving yards per game, three red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 38.1% first-read share. In those two games, Douglas has been the WR38 and WR60 in weekly scoring. He's a volume-based flex option with a solid matchup this week. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the fourth-most yards per target and the second-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 7, Antonio Williams has been the WR24 in fantasy points per game, but much of that is on the strength of last week's game, as he was the WR6 in weekly scoring. Williams has at least 10.4 PPR points in three of his last four games, though. Since Week 7, he has had an 18.9% target share with 1.88 YPRR and a 23.4% first-read share. Last week, he had a massive 31.4% target share with 3.39 YPRR, nine receptions, 122 receiving yards, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 40.9% first-read share. Williams is a strong fantasy option again this week. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Denzel Boston has been listed as questionable for Week 12, but he hasn't practiced all week (quad). I consider him closer to doubtful than questionable this week. Boston has been dinged up, and this might finally be the week to sit him down and let him heal up some. Make plans that he'll be out this week, and if he plays, it'll be a nice surprise for fantasy. Boston is the WR33 in fantasy points per game with an 18.3% target share, 1.56 YPRR, nine red zone targets, 16 deep targets, and a 21.8% first-read share. Across their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. If Boston plays, he's a strong flex who could post WR2 numbers this week.

In his first game back, Jacory Croskey-Merritt was the RB12 for the week. He had 15 touches, 77 total yards, and a score. Bill led the backfield with a 42.2% snap rate, 50% of the rushing attempts, and a 21.4% route share (8.6% target share). Bill wasn't amazing with his workload, though, with zero explosive runs, 2.00 yards after contact per attempt, and a 15% missed tackle rate. I expect him to lead the backfield in touches this week, but Austin Ekeler and Rachaad White will be involved. Bill is a touchdown-dependent flex. Over their last five games, Arizona has tightened up their run defense, allowing the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the tenth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the 12th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Since Week 7, Chig Okonkwo has been the TE16 in fantasy points per game, with two outings with at least double-digit PPR points. Since Week 7, he has had an 18.2% target share with 1.66 YPRR, 44.8 receiving yards per game, one red zone target, two deep targets, and a 21.3% first-read share. Okonkwo is a strong streaming option this week. Over their last five games, Arizona has allowed the 11th-most yards per target, the most receiving touchdowns (tied), and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Jordyn Tyson had a banner Week 10. Tyson was the WR12 while seeing a 72.1% snap share and route share. He gobbled up a 37.1% target share with 80 receiving yards (2.58 YPRR), one red zone target, two deep targets, and a 41.7% first-read share. Tyson also had a 23.1% designed target rate that week. Well, Week 11 didn't build upon that big game. Last week, Tyson had only a 49.3% snap rate, a 42.3% route share, a 2.3% target share, one reception, six receiving yards, and a 7.1% first-read share. Kellen Moore said that Tyson's playing time decrease was merely the result of them utilizing no huddle and not switching out personnel, which does track with the fact that they were second in no huddle plays last week with 15 behind only the Titans. I lean that Tyson will have a bounce-back game this week. He could be heavily utilized again if DJ Turner is shadowing Chris Olave. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game to slot receivers while also giving up the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Since Week 7, Aaron Jones has been the 1B in the Minny backfield with a 37.2% snap rate, a 33.3% rushing share, and a 24.4% route share (3.8% target share). He has averaged 8.6 touches and 37 total yards. Jones has only 2.03 yards after contact per attempt and a 13% missed tackle rate this season. Father Time and playing through injuries have hurt his efficiency. Jones is only a low-end flex play this week with a good matchup. Over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the 11th-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards after contact per attempt, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

In his last two games, with Baker Mayfield actually throwing the ball, Emeka Egbuka has had a saddening 15.4% target share with 0.98 YPRR, 28 receiving yards per game, one red zone target, three deep targets, and a 17.8% first-read share. Egbuka is a middling flex play this week. At this point, I just don't have much faith in Egbuka. The matchup isn't overwhelming. Over their last five games, Carolina has ranked 16th in yards per target and 18th in receiving fantasy points per game allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

Last week, Ladd McConkey had two scores and finished as the WR7 for the week. He had a 77.2% snap rate, a 78.1% route share, a 33.3% target share, 1.48 YPRR (37 receiving yards), two red zone targets, and a 27.3% first-read share. When McConkey is active, the Bolts' passing attack has condensed around him. He has essentially been the only viable receiving option. It has been either him or Tre Harris, depending on McConkey's status. McConkey could have another strong game in Week 12. Over their last five games, the Pats have allowed the third-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 5, Jaylen Waddle has been the WR62 in fantasy points per game with a 15% target share, 1.82 YPRR, a 58.5% route share, and a 25% first-read share. In that span, he has only one game with double-digit PPR points. It has been a lost season. I don't expect better results this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 7, Dylan Sampson has averaged 8.8 touches and 57.8 total yards as the RB33 in fantasy points per game. He's a viable PPR flex again this week. In these four games, he has had a 49.2% route share with an 11.5% target share. In their last five games, the Raiders have faced the fewest targets to running backs while ranking 16th in yards per target allowed to the position.

Since Week 4, Khalil Shakir has been the WR31 in fantasy points per game with a 17.1% target share, 2.53 YPRR, three red zone targets, four deep targets, and an 18.7% first-read share. The Chiefs have the seventh-highest two-high rate in the NFL (59.2%). Since Week 8, against two high, Shakir has had a 19% TPRR with 2.45 YPRR. Josh Allen could lean on Shakir this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has ranked 16th in yards per target against slot receivers while allowing the 12th-most receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

Bryce Young's poor play has capsized Jalen Coker's season. Since Week 7, he has been the WR85 in fantasy points per game. During that stretch, he hasn't had a single game with double-digit PPR points. Since Week 7, he has had a 13.5% target share with 0.77 YPRR, 24.2 receiving yards per game, five red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 20.7% first-read share. Sit Coker this week. Over their last five games, the Bucs have allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position.

Brenton Strange is the TE17 in fantasy points per game. Among 51 qualifying tight ends, Strange is 20th in target share (13.9%), 16th in YPRR (1.67), and 20th in first-read share (14.4%). He has five red zone targets and two deep targets this season. Strange could be a TE1 this week, operating as the number two option in the passing game with Parker Washington out. Over their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the 13th-most yards per target, the sixth-most receiving fantasy points per game, and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Josh Downs didn't see a massive jump in his playing time, with a 31.7% route share while seeing a 12.5% target share (38% TPRR) with 59 receiving yards (4.54 YPRR), and a 16.1% first-read share. In his last two games with the Chiefs, he has had an insane 48% TPRR with 5.33 YPRR. Those numbers aren't sustainable, but I do expect Downs to be highly utilized when he is on the field. Downs has been running nearly all of his routes from the slot (90.5%). Buffalo presents a sizable challenge for Downs. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Downs is a risky but viable flex.

Braelon Allen is a solid flex play this week. Last week, he lost more work to Breece Hall, but the matchup is quite nice this week, so he should get some early down work with the hopes of a score. Last week, Allen had a 37.3% snap rate, 43.2% of the rushing work, a 21.7% route share, and a 4.8% target share. Allen had 17 touches and 84 total yards. That's an RB2 stat line. He was RB23 in weekly scoring. Allen's per-touch metrics remain stellar with a 15% explosive run rate, 2.69 yards after contact per attempt, and a 19% missed tackle rate. Miami's run defense remains pitiful. Over their last five games, they have allowed the eighth-highest explosive run rate, the tenth-most rushing yards over expectation per attempt, and the highest missed tackle rate.

Dalton Kincaid missed last week's game (thumb/ankle). He practiced on a limited basis this week and has been listed as questionable. Kincaid is the TE9 in fantasy points per game, but that is more of an indictment of the tight end position this season than a positive for Kincaid. He has managed less than eight PPR points in five games this season. Since Week 8, he has had a 51.7% snap rate, a 51.6% route share, a 14% target share, 3.51 YPRR, 57.3 receiving yards per game, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and an 18.3 first-read share. He could be a TE1 this week, but he doesn't have a smash matchup this week. Over their last five games, the Chiefs have ranked 15th in yards per target allowed to tight ends while giving up the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Since Week 9, Kenneth Gainwell has been the RB26 in fantasy points per game (PPR), averaging eight touches and 67.5 total yards. He has essentially been the Dylan Sampson of Tampa Bay. Most of his production has come through the passing game with 51.5 receiving yards per game, a 12.3% target share, 4.12 YPRR, and a red zone target. Gainwell is a decent PPR flex this week. Across their last five games, Carolina has allowed two receiving touchdowns to backs and the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game to the position.

Since Week 7, Jordan Mason has been the 1A in the Minnesota backfield, averaging 11.8 touches and 44.6 total yards. Mason, during this stretch, has had a 46.8% snap rate, 50.5% of the rushing work, and a 26.1% route share (4.4% target share). Mason hasn't been efficient as a runner this season with only 2.01 yards after contact per attempt and a 15% missed tackle rate, but that might not matter this week. With his combo of volume and a nice matchup, he could be a decent flex/RB2 this week. Over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the highest explosive run rate, the 11th-highest rushing success rate, the second-most yards after contact per attempt, and the ninth-highest missed tackle rate.

Adonai Mitchell is the WR58 this season, with two games with more than ten PPR points. Mitchell has a 20.4% target share, 1.93 YPRR, five red zone targets, 17 deep targets (17.8 aDOT), and a 24% first-read share. 37.8% of his target volume has been via deep passing. This matchup lines up well for Mitchell to have another spike-week performance. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the seventh-most yards per target and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. In the same span of games, Miami has allowed the ninth-most deep passing yards, the ninth-highest passer rating to downfield passing, and the seventh-highest deep passing completion rate. Mitchell is a boom-or-bust flex option who could boom this week.

Justice Hill is a viable flex option. Over the last two games, he has averaged nine touches and 67 total yards. With Jacoby Brissett under center, he has had a 14% target share with 30.5 receiving yards per game, 1.42 YPRR, and two red zone targets. Across their last five games, Houston has allowed the eighth-most receiving fantasy points per game to running backs.

Since Week 8, Mike Gesicki has had a 59.8% route share, a 9.9% target share, 1.66 YPRR, 43.2 receiving yards per game, two red zone targets, a deep target, and an 11.1% first-read share. Gesicki is on the streaming radar again this week. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Poor Tyler Warren. Warren is an awesome talent that is languishing inside this broken Indy offense for the rest of the season. Since Week 10, Warren has had a 13.7% target share, 0.49 YPRR, only 23 receiving yards, and a hollow 14.3% first-read share. Sadly, I don't see this week as a possible turnaround spot for Warren. New York has shut down tight ends. Over their last five games, they have allowed the third-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Since Week 9, Xavier Hutchinson has had a 15.7% target share with 1.10 YPRR, 33.3 receiving yards per game, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and an 18.6% first-read share. He has had at least 11.9 PPR points in two of these three games. He's flex-viable again this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Since Week 5, Ryan Flournoy has been the WR36 in fantasy points per game with an 11.9% target share, 1.69 YPRR, eight red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 10.7% first-read share. Since Week 5, Philly has had the eighth-highest single-high rate (57.4%). Since Week 5, against single-high, Flournoy has seen his TPRR jump to 16% with a STRONG 2.22 YPRR. Flournoy could have another big game this week. Over their last five games, Philly has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Since Week 9, Tank Dell has remained a part-time player for Houston. He has had a 45.4% snap rate, a 54% route share, a 16.7% target share, 51 receiving yards per game, 2.51 YPRR, one red zone target, five deep targets, and a 27.1% first-read share. Dell is a risky but flex-viable option this week. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 5, Kyle Pitts has been the TE8 in fantasy points per game with a 16.5% target share, 1.31 YPRR, seven red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.9% first-read share. Pitts hasn't scored a touchdown in his last three games, and only once in his last four games has he surpassed 40 receiving yards. He'll need a touchdown to be a TE1 again this week. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target to tight ends while ranking 16th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position.

Since Week 7, Rico Dowdle has been the RB36 in fantasy points per game, while averaging 11.5 touches and 52.5 total yards. During this four-game span, he has had a 43% snap rate, 32.1% of the rushing workload, and a 41.2% route share (tying Jaylen Warren). He has split the red zone rushing work evenly, with Warren seeing seven red zone rushing attempts. Among 55 qualifying rushers, Dowdle is ninth in explosive run rate, 11th in yards after contact per attempt, and 13th in missed tackle rate. If Mike McCarthy can convince Aaron Rodgers that their best course of action is to run the ball, Rico Dowdle should have a nice week as a flex option. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards after contact per attempt, and the fourth-highest missed tackle rate.

Woody Marks is working through the concussion protocol. I expect him to play this week after opening with a full practice. In Weeks 1-4, Marks had a 44.3% snap rate, 31.1% of the rushing workload, and a 35.9% route share (5.9% target share). I'm not sure if Marks will see that much work this week with David Montgomery back and coming off a successful workhorse game. With Marks' workload up in the air, I'm leaving him on the bench this week with a horrible matchup incoming. Over their last five games, Baltimore has allowed the ninth-lowest explosive run rate, the sixth-lowest rushing yards over expectation per attempt and missed tackle rate, and the fifth-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

In his two games with Joe Milton under center, Dallas Goedert has had a 12.7% target share with 1.63 YPRR, 44 receiving yards per game, one deep target, and only a 7.7% first-read share. He hasn't been a huge part of the offense, with Milton targeting the wide receivers more. I'm expecting a quiet game for Goedert this week. Across their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, Chimere Dike led the team with a 23.3% target share with 2.65 YPRR (69 receiving yards), one deep target, and a 37.5% first-read share as the team's starting slot receiver (65.4% slot). Dike was the WR24 in weekly scoring. Calvin Ridley and Elic Ayomanor split the other perimeter spot opposite Carnell Tate last week, and Dike was a full-time player with an 82.5% snap rate and 72.2% route share. Dike is an interesting flex option this week. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the 14th-most receiving fantasy points per game and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Over the last two weeks, with Fernando Mendoza under center, Tre Tucker has had a 15.2% target share with 0.83 YPRR, 29.5 receiving yards per game, zero red zone targets, four deep targets, and an 18.5% first-read share. Sit Tucker this week. Across their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Tyler Allgeier isn't worth considering for a flex spot this week. Arizona's offense has been dead in the water, the matchup is horrible, and he's not getting enough volume to make an impact for fantasy. Since Week 10, Allgeier has averaged six rushing attempts and 18.5 rushing yards. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the eighth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, the tenth-fewest rushing yards, and the 14th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

DK Metcalf got ejected from last week's game. It doesn't sound like he will face a suspension, so I'm projecting him to play this week. Metcalf is the WR47 in fantasy points per game. I'm not projecting Patrick Surtain to follow DK Metcalf, but I wouldn't be shocked if it happens in Week 12, either. Surtain has shadowed twice this season, following Davante Adams and Tetairoa McMillan on 76.5-90% of their routes. Adams cooked him for six receptions and 88 receiving yards, and McMillan had 56 receiving yards and a score. Metcalf has a 20.2% target share with 1.27 YPRR, five red zone targets, 22 deep targets, and a 27.3% first-read share. This week, he'll face a Denver secondary that, since Week 8, has utilized single high at the fourth-highest rate (63.4%). This season, Metcalf has been horrible against every coverage, but against single high he has gotten a bump with a 23% TPRR and 1.47 YPRR. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the 11th-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. I'm not expecting much from Metcalf this week.

Last week, Keenan Allen had a 54.7% snap rate, a 64.3% route share, a 14.8% target share, 38 receiving yards (2.11 YPRR), and a 21.1% first-read share (second on the team). I expect Keenan Allen's usage to sit in this area code again this week, which leaves him as an uninspiring flex play who is best left on the bench. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Across their last five games, Dallas has held slot receivers to the eighth-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Sit Lemon this week.

Since Week 5, DeMario Douglas has been the WR19 in fantasy points per game. During this span, he has had a 71.9% route share, a 16.7% target share, 2.28 YPRR, 59.3 receiving yards per game, two red zone targets, six deep targets, and a 17.9% first-read share. Douglas is flex-viable again this week. Across their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

Bam Knight isn't on the flex radar this week. Since Week 10, Bam Knight has been leading the backfield in usage, but he's not getting enough volume to matter for fantasy. Arizona's offense has also been dead in the water. Since Week 10, Knight has averaged 6.5 touches and 32 total yards while averaging 51.7% of the snaps with a 33.3% route share. Washington's run defense has been really tough. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the seventh-lowest explosive run rate, the eighth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, the tenth-fewest rushing yards, and the 14th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

After a big game in Week 10 for Mark Andrews, he disappeared last week. Andrews had only an 8.1% target share with 14 receiving yards (0.56 YPRR) and zero first reads. Since Week 10, Andrews has a 12.8% target share, 1.71 YPRR, 48 receiving yards per game, one red zone target, and a 9.3% first-read share. Sit Andrews this week. I'm expecting another quiet game. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the ninth-fewest receiving fantasy points per game and fantasy points per opportunity.

Darren Waller has a 55.7% route share, a 9.9% target share, 1.58 YPRR, 36.5 receiving yards per game, five red zone targets, six deep targets, and an 11.6% first-read share. Waller is the TE16 in fantasy points per game with two TE1 finishes in weekly scoring. Waller is a streaming option again this week. Over their last five games, Tampa Bay has allowed the seventh-most yards per target and the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Over the last two games, Devaughn Vele has transitioned to perimeter wide receiver for New Orleans while earning an 11.5% target share with 1.15 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 10.5% first-read share. Vele could see a healthy target volume this week if Chris Olave is followed by DJ Turner as he and Jordyn Tyson handle the heavy lifting. Vele is a flex option this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Dalton Schultz hasn't been part of the offense. Since Week 9, he has had a 56.6% route share with only a 5.9% target share, 31.3 receiving yards per game, 1.00 YPRR, and a 5.1% first-read share. Schultz isn't on the fantasy radar until his usage changes in this passing offense.

Last week, despite the return of Roman Wilson, Germie Bernard remained a full-time player. In the first half, with DK Metcalf also on the field, Bernard had a 91.3% route share. With Michael Pittman Jr. returning this week, I expect Bernard to remain in the starting lineup, but I wouldn't be shocked if his route share dips some. Since Week 5, Bernard has been the WR43 in fantasy points per game with a 20.4% target share, 1.31 YPRR, eight red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 22.1% first-read share. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per target and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to wide receivers. Bernard is a deep league desperation flex only.

Alvin Kamara isn't on the flex radar anymore. Last week, he played only seven snaps with three opportunities. Yes, he scored a touchdown, but he finished with only two touches and two total yards. Kamara is droppable.

I don't know if anyone is still holding onto any hope for Courtland Sutton this season, but I figured I'd include his outlook for Week 12, anyway. Since Week 5, Sutton has been the WR65 in fantasy points per game with one double-digit PPR outing. During this span, he has had a 13.4% target share with 1.18 YPRR, four red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 16% first-read share. Sit Sutton again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Since Week 4, Hunter Henry has been the TE13 in fantasy points per game with five games of at least double-digit PPR points. In his last two games, Hunter Henry has seen his playing time cut some as he has played through a foot issue. He isn't on the injury report, but that doesn't mean the foot is 100% healthy. Since Week 9, Henry has had a 48.8% route share with an 8.7% target share, 1.43 YPRR, one red zone target, and an 11.15 first-read share. I hope his playing time increases this week, but we'll have to see. If Henry is playing a near full-time role, he could return TE1 production this week. That's assuming that Tommy DeVito isn't a full-blown dumpster fire again. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

After a busy game in Week 10, Ja'Kobi Lane's usage tailed off last week. His route share dropped to 51.3% as Rashod Bateman stood up as the WR2 for the offense. Last week, Rashod Bateman had an 84.6% route share, a 16.2% target share, 67 receiving yards (2.03 YPRR), one red zone target, two deep targets, and an 11.1% first-read share. Bateman is a deeper league flex option only. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the 14th-most yards per target to perimeter wide receivers while giving up the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

The last time Mason Taylor faced this pass defense, he was the TE2 in weekly scoring. I'm not saying that will happen this week, but Taylor is a strong streaming candidate. Since Week 6, Taylor has had a 67.2% snap rate, a 56.2% route share, a 13.4% target share, 1.44 YPRR, five red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 14.2% first-read share. Across their last six games, Miami has ranked 15th in yards per target allowed to tight ends while also giving up the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Last week, Evan Engram exploded as the TE5 for the week. Knowing Sean Payton, I'd be wrong to assume this, BUT it would be wise for Denver to keep feeding Engram this week. Last week, Engram had a 44.3% snap rate, a 67.6% route share, a 25.7% target share, 74 receiving yards (2.96 YPRR), two deep targets, and a 29.4% first-read share. One of Pittsburgh's weaknesses has been defending tight ends all season. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Engram is a risky but high-upside streaming option this week.

Last week, with Joe Milton chucking it, Darius Cooper had a 23.8% target share, 59 receiving yards (2.57 YPRR), one deep target, and a 22.2% first-read share. He operated as the clear number two in the passing attack behind DeVonta Smith. In his two games with Milton, Cooper has had a 21.8% target share with 1.33 YPRR, four deep targets, and a 28.2% first-read share. Cooper is a flex option that could bear fruit if Milton can get him the ball this week. Across their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.

Ted Hurst busted out with two touchdowns last week as the WR5 in weekly scoring. Hurst led the team with a 21.2% target share, 2.07 YPRR, 56 receiving yards, and a 24% first-read share. Hurst has two end zone targets and one deep target. I'm curious if this is the breakout game for Hurst. Among 100 qualifying receivers this season, he is 27th in route win rate. The team has spoken about getting him more involved and coming out of the bye with Emeka Egbuka still struggling this could create an interesting avenue for Hurst to ascend. Last week, Hurst had a 63.1% snap rate which was his highest snap rate since Week 3. He's an interesting flex with some upside this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has ranked 16th in yards per target and 18th in receiving fantasy points per game allowed to perimeter wide receivers.

Rachaad White is practicing in full to open this week (heel). The Commanders are utilizing a three-headed committee, and White was on the outside looking in last week. White played only 20.3% of the snaps with zero rushing attempts and a 16.7% route share. White could play more this week if the heel is feeling better, but the matchup is rough. There's no reason to absorb the risk with his playing time up in the air and a bad matchup incoming. Over their last five games, Arizona has tightened up their run defense, allowing the fourth-lowest explosive run rate, the tenth-fewest yards before contact per attempt, and the 12th-fewest yards after contact per attempt.

Last week, Jack Bech was the WR5 in weekly scoring. Over the last two games, he has had 15 targets, a 22.7% target share, 1.63 YPRR, three red zone targets, and a 25.9% first-read share. His volume will take a hit with Brock Bowers back, but he could still be a flex option this week. Across their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the 12th-most yards per target to slot receivers.

Last week, Tai Felton had a 27.9% target share, 42 receiving yards (1.27 YPRR), one red zone target, one deep target, and a 26.5% first-read share. Overall this season, he has been an afterthought with a 15% TPRR, 0.79 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 9.7% first-read share. Felton could be a flex option if he sees even half that volume this week, though. Atlanta has been horrible at defending perimeter wide receivers this season. Over their last five games, they have allowed the second-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Since Week 10, Anthony Gould has had a 13.7% target share with 2.00 YPRR, 38 receiving yards per game, one deep target, and a 20% first-read share. Gould is a deep-league desperation flex only. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target and the 12th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.

If JJ McCarthy is able to hook up with a receiver downfield this week, It'll likely be Malik Nabers or Darnell Mooney. Since Week 7, Mooney has had an 11.5% target share, 0.63 YPRR, a 17.4 aDOT, and a 12.9% first-read share. 46.6% of his targets have been downfield in this span. Across Indy's last five games, they have allowed the fifth-most deep passing yards, the third-highest passer rating to deep passing, and the 11th-highest deep passing success rate. Mooney is a deep-league flex. Also, in their last five games, Indy has allowed the tenth-most yards per target to slot receivers while ranking 17th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to the position.

Last week, Michael Pittman Jr. practiced in full on Thursday and Friday (foot) before sitting out. I expect him to play this week, but I'm not plugging him into any fantasy lineups. This week, he'll face a Denver secondary that, since Week 8, has utilized single high at the fourth-highest rate (63.4%). This season, against single high, Pittman Jr. has only an 11% TPRR and 0.88 YPRR. Even if he is able to buck that trend, the matchup is horrible. Across their last five games, Denver has allowed the 11th-fewest yards per target and the tenth-fewest points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Sit Pittman Jr. this week.

Harrison Wallace is a deep-league flex this week. Last week, he was second on the team with a 19.4% target share, 57 receiving yards (2.11 YPRR), two deep targets, and a 22.7% first-read share. Wallace was third on the team with a 75% route share while running 55.6% of his routes from the slot. Wallace is a PPR volume-driven flex option only. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers.
